html:
In about 552 monks brought silkworm eggs in secret from Central Asia to Constantinople, so that the Byzantine Empire could make its own silk. The story comes from the historian Procopius.

Silk was a costly luxury in Rome and Byzantium, and all of it came from the East along the Silk Road. Persia sat in the middle and took a share of every bale, which galled the emperor Justinian. According to Procopius, monks who had lived in a land called Serinda offered to fetch the eggs. They are said to have hidden them in hollow canes. Serinda was probably in Sogdia or the Tarim Basin, where silk making had already spread from China.

The new industry grew in Greece and Syria and became a state monopoly. China lost its sole hold on the craft, though Chinese silk stayed in demand for centuries. See also the same story seen from Europe.
sum: In about 552 monks brought silkworm eggs in secret from Central Asia to Constantinople, so that the Byzantine Empire could make its own silk. The story comes from the historian Procopius.
